prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that enabled incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: GLP-1 is the clearest full arc on the shortlist, from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect to the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and to drugs with large, independently replicated outcome benefits in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease. All six of us ranked it first, but that agreement is not itself the argument. The argument is that the physiology was original, the mechanism is stable, the clinical confirmation is extensive and current, and the recognition is timely. On reflection I am moving my opening trio from Knudsen to Mojsov. The prize is for the discovery of the hormone biology and the identification of the active peptide, and that is what Drucker, Holst and Mojsov each supplied. Knudsen's drug design is decisive for the products but is a development contribution that sits better outside a three-person cap.
statement.case_against: The main weakness is attribution, not merit. Priority for identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1 fragment is contested between Mojsov, Habener and others, and Habener is not on the credited list. A three-person cap also excludes Knudsen, whose long-acting analogues are the reason the science reached patients at scale. If the committee judges that translation is the core of the achievement, the trio I now favour reads as a physiology prize and leaves out the drug builders. Mojsov's relative weight is the least certain element of the set.

responses.point: Knudsen's work on long-acting analogues is decisive for the drugs but is more a development contribution, so a fair trio is plausible with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov.
responses.response: I partly changed my opening view because of this. I had included Knudsen because the translational step is what turned the physiology into a therapy. I now agree that the discovery claim is better carried by the three who defined the biology and the active peptide. I qualify it, though: if the citation names therapy, as it should, it must say so explicitly, so that the omission of Knudsen is not read as dismissing the drug-development achievement. I also differ on your second-ranked B001. Nusinersen is a clean RNA-to-drug story, but it is a single disease, and its scale of impact does not match that of incretin therapy.

responses.point: TNF blockade (Feldmann and Maini) is a clear translational milestone for chronic inflammatory disease, mature and not premature, with a clean two-person attribution.
responses.response: I take the clean attribution seriously, and it is a real advantage over CAR-T and optogenetics. But I do not rank B036 ahead of B039 or B014. Anti-TNF is a landmark for a defined disease class, and I am less convinced that the discovery is as conceptually original as its clinical consequence is large. The synovial cytokine-network proof of concept built on earlier cytokine biology, and the antibody engineering was done by others. I would like to hear more on why you rank it above cGAS-STING in discovery terms, since you also ranked that third.

responses.point: CAR-T (B039) is mature in haematological cancers with approved products and multi-year follow-up, but the original chimeric receptor concept came from Eshhar and others who are not credited, so credit could be disputed.
responses.response: I agree that this is the serious obstacle and I think it is more than a footnote. The credited trio rewards June and Sadelain for costimulatory engineering and clinical proof and Rosenberg for adoptive cell transfer. A citation that honours these without the originators of the chimeric receptor concept would be open to challenge on priority. This is why I keep B039 as an alternative rather than a co-equal second part. I also resist treating long remissions beyond a decade as settled for the whole field, because the evidence on durability and toxicity is still accumulating outside B-cell malignancies.

responses.point: The unfolded protein response (Mori and Walter) is a compact, thoroughly confirmed new principle of ER-to-nucleus signalling, and a fair two-person prize that is not premature.
responses.response: I agree on the quality of the science and on the two-person fairness, and I ranked B014 third myself. I would not advance it over B027 for this year, because its translational payoff is still modest. If the committee wants a two-part prize, B014 is the cleanest basic-science partner for GLP-1. I note that Ron and Kaufman are outside the credited names, so I rely on Walter and Mori only because the file restricts me to them, and I would not call the attribution fully settled.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1 peptide can be weighted against Habener's, who is not credited on the ballot.
Whether omitting Knudsen from the credited trio is defensible, and whether the citation can acknowledge therapy without naming her.
Whether a two-part prize (GLP-1 with UPR or CAR-T) is better than a single GLP-1 prize, given that B039 has an unresolved Eshhar credit issue and B014 has modest clinical payoff.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I have co-authored with Linnarsson and Frisen, and my research touches RNA processing, but none of the shortlisted candidates involves a documented collaboration or institutional tie of mine.
